llm_evidence: ["To me, democracy means that everyone has a say in how they are governed, and that decisions are made through fair processes. It includes having free and fair elections, and protecting the rights of minorities. I think about things like checks and balances and how laws are made to ensure everyone is treated fairly.", "Well, when I see issues where the system isn't fully inclusive or where it takes too long to resolve cases, it makes me think about how true to the ideals of democracy it really is. It should be about more than just majority rule, it should be fair for everyone, so any voice counts."]

["It's about having a fair and transparent system where everyone can participate and hold those in power accountable. That's a big part of what democracy is all about.", "When decisions are heavily influenced by popular opinion rather than fairness, it can lead to issues. That's when I think it crossed into something that wasn't really good for the majority or for minorities who often ended up being affected negatively."]

["I think everyone should get a say in how they're governed. It's about fairness and equality.", "Sometimes quick results are needed, especially for businesses or families who are living through it. But at the same time, I think democracy should also strive for fairness and good policies for everyone in the long run."]

["Democracy to me means having a say in how things are run and having fair elections. But you know, I've seen how slow and frustrating politics can be at times. I'd just like to see someone who gets things done without all the back and forth.", "It feels like if we just had someone clear as to what needs to happen, things would move faster. A clear leader fits right into democracy because it's about having a fair process where everyone can voice their opinions, but someone needs to make the final call."]

["To me, democracy means everyone gets a say, not just the politicians and judges. I think the will of the majority should always settle things; that's how you keep things fair and honest, in my eyes.", "Compromise and finding common ground help balance different perspectives in a democracy because it allows everyone to have their say, and it often leads to better decisions that are more accepted."]

["To me, democracy means that we get to have a say in how we're ruled, not just the politicians and judges who sometimes seem to ignore what many ordinary folks want. The will of the majority should always win in the end, so that everyone's voice is heard, not just a few who might be in the spotlight.", "The will of the majority is heard in practice through things like voting on important issues, having laws made based on what the majority decides, and having some kind of checks or balances to keep power from getting too concentrated."]
["I don't know if that works, I don't know, that's how it is sometimes.", "Sometimes policymakers may overlook certain views for various reasons."]

["Democracy means to me a system where people have a say in how they're governed, kind of like a big decision-making party where everyone gets a voice.", "Sometimes the decisions felt more influenced by money or power rather than what benefits everyone."]

["I think treating everyone equally is just fair, you know? People should be treated the same no matter who they are. Fair pay is important because if someone works hard, they should get a decent wage so they can support themselves and their families. It's a basic part of making sure the system works for everyone.", "I remember when teaching was a bit lower paid compared to other professions. That wasn't fair, and sometimes it lead to burnout. There are also places where people with the same skill level are paid differently based on their job titles, which can be seen as not fair. That's why fair pay is so crucial—it affects people’s well-being and the overall fairness of the system."]

["Democracy to me is about everyone being treated fairly and equally, with fair wages to support a decent life, and having access to good public services like healthcare and education. It's about making sure the government listens to all of us, not just the rich and powerful.", "I've seen how kids from poorer areas sometimes don't have the same opportunities. For instance, some don't have access to books or computers at home, so they can't do their homework. It can be really tough, kind of like if you went to school with all the toys and games, and your friends went with nothing but their hands. That could put some kids behind. Plus, a school with less funding might not have as many teachers or specialists, so they might not get the help they need to catch up on subjects like math or science. It's like a race, and some kids have more energy to start with."]

["I prefer things to be predictable and work more or less the same way they've always been. Things changing too much or unpredictably can throw me off for sure.", "Uncertainty really did unsettle me during the financial crisis. The markets were going up and down quickly, and people were making decisions that seemed really uncertain and uncontrolled. That really threw me off a bit."]
